 Between one client and the next
 The phone rings at ten past, and you cannot pick up 
 1 During a session
 Your phone rings while you are with a client. New enquiries get voicemail, and you spend your break returning calls.
 2 The call you never hear about
 Asking for help takes courage. A person who reaches voicemail often tries the next name on the directory, and you never know they called.
 3 What your day looks like instead
 Every call answered warmly and briefly, first appointments offered from your diary, and a short message waiting for you between sessions.
 Where it stops
 What it will not do 
 This is a reception tool and nothing more. Every line below is agreed and tested with your practice before a real caller hears it.
 No clinical advice
 It gives no clinical advice and makes no assessment, however a caller phrases the question. Anything of that kind becomes a message for you.
 No asking why
 It does not ask why someone is seeking help. A name, a way to reach them and a time that suits is all it needs from them.
 A caller who appears at risk
 It gives 999 and Samaritans on 116 123, then alerts you straight away. It does not attempt to counsel anybody.
 What it costs
 Priced for a private practice, not a hospital trust 
 The receptionist starts at £497 to set up and £97 a month. A website chatbot sits beside it for practices that also take enquiries online, and what you are buying is put in writing before you commit.

 Getting it running
 Agreed with you, then tested with you 
 01 Tell Andy how you work
 Your hours, your approach and the way you like first appointments offered. He drafts the wording from that.
 02 Read every word
 You see how it tells callers it is an AI and what it says to someone in crisis, then change whatever does not sound like your practice.
 03 Ring it, then go live
 You hear it yourself before any client does. Only after that do calls reach it and messages start to arrive between sessions.

 Who sets it up
 Andy Norman is no clinician, and it will not act like one 
 Andy runs Antek Automation from Andover in Hampshire, following more than 30 years in field service and managed print. As a Certified Retell AI Partner he sets up and tunes each receptionist himself.
 With no clinical training of his own, he treats what your callers hear as your decision. His part is making sure it says exactly that, and stops there.

 Before you decide
 What therapists ask about it first 
 Will callers know it is an AI?
 Yes. It says so at the start of every call, in words you have agreed, so nobody believes they are speaking to you or to a member of staff.
 What happens if someone is in crisis?
 A caller who appears at risk is given 999 and Samaritans on 116 123, and you are alerted straight away. It never tries to assess or counsel them. That wording is agreed with your practice and tested before it takes a live call.
 Where are call recordings stored and for how long?
 This page cannot give you a blanket answer, and it would be wrong to guess. Where the data is held and how long it is kept are confirmed and written into your scope before anything goes live, so you can review both first.
 Do I have to record calls?
 That gets settled with you during setup instead of being assumed. Whatever you decide goes into your scope, along with what callers are told about it.
 Can it book into my practice software?
 It depends on the software. Which systems it connects to is confirmed and written into your scope before launch. If yours cannot be linked, it takes the details and passes them to you to book by hand.
 Is it just an answering service for therapists?
 It covers that ground, then goes further by explaining how you work and offering a first appointment, where a message service would simply take a name and number.
 Could a larger practice use it?
 Yes. An AI receptionist for clinics with several practitioners answers in the practice name in the same way, and who receives each message is agreed during setup.
 Stay with your client. The phone is covered.

 About AI Receptionist for Therapists
 AI Receptionist for Therapists is a service from Antek Automation, a sole trader in Andover led by Andy Norman, for counsellors, psychotherapists, physiotherapists and small private practices across the UK. AI for therapists can mean many things. Here it means one thing: the phone gets answered while you work. Read about the AI voice assistants behind it on the main site.

 Where he draws the line
 Andy is not a therapist. The words your receptionist uses are agreed and tested with you, and he will not add anything that could be heard as advice.
